content.value_statement: Ruby projects often need type signatures without changing source code. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to infer RBS and validate the result.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes Ruby classes, modules, methods, constants, and instance variables.
Creates RBS files under sig/ using the Ruby source structure.
Uses bundled RBS syntax and library examples as references.
Reduces unnecessary untyped entries when source evidence supports better types.
Runs rbs validate and optional Steep checks when the project supports them.
Includes guidance for Data and Struct signatures.
limitations: Does not update existing RBS signatures automatically.
Should not execute Ruby application code to infer types.
May need user input when source evidence is incomplete.

use_cases.title: Add First RBS Files
use_cases.description: Generate initial signatures for Ruby classes that do not have RBS coverage.

use_cases.title: Improve Type Coverage
use_cases.description: Replace broad or missing types by reading source, tests, and call sites.

use_cases.title: Validate Library Signatures
use_cases.description: Check generated signatures against RBS rules and optional Steep checks.

prompt_templates.title: Create Starter RBS
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one Ruby file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate RBS signatures for <path>. Analyze classes, modules, constants, and methods. Put new files under sig/ and avoid untyped when possible.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Inferred Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a draft signature for better precision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the generated RBS for <path>. Replace unnecessary untyped entries using method bodies, tests, and call sites. Explain any remaining uncertainty.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Signatures
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the RBS validation workflow for the generated signatures. Fix shape errors and repeat until validation passes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Steep Assurance
prompt_templates.prompt: If the project uses Steep, run the type check after validation. Fix RBS issues without changing Steepfile or executing application code.

output_examples.input: User asks for RBS for app/models/order.rb.
output_examples.output: Creates a matching signature file, lists covered declarations, explains inferred types, and reports validation status.

output_examples.input: User asks to remove untyped from a draft signature.
output_examples.output: Reviews source and tests, replaces broad types with concrete Ruby and domain types, and lists places needing user confirmation.

output_examples.input: User asks to validate generated signatures in a Steep project.
output_examples.output: Runs the validation steps, summarizes errors found, updates signatures, and reports remaining Steep issues.

best_practices: Read the Ruby source and nearby tests before writing signatures.
Use bundled RBS references for syntax and core library shapes.
Validate generated files before considering the task complete.
anti_patterns: Do not run application code to discover types.
Do not leave untyped when call sites reveal a better type.
Do not edit Steepfile to hide signature errors.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates RBS signature files for Ruby source files without changing the Ruby code.

faq.question: Does it support existing RBS files?
faq.answer: It focuses on creating signatures from scratch and does not automatically update existing signatures.

faq.question: Does it run Ruby application code?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly tells the agent not to run project Ruby code for type discovery.

faq.question: When does it use Steep?
faq.answer: It uses Steep only when the project has both a Steepfile and the steep gem in the Gemfile.

faq.question: How does it avoid untyped signatures?
faq.answer: It reads source, tests, and call examples to infer more precise types when evidence is available.

faq.question: Can it help with Struct and Data classes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes specific reference guidance for Data and Struct signatures.
